title: Seek, do, teach (Ezra 7:10)
hookLine: Ezra the scribe set his heart to seek the law, do it, and teach it
carry: study begins as a direction you set inside

lines: A LINE OF FATHERS, BACK TO AARON.
cards: The book that bears his name runs for chapters before Ezra himself walks in. When he does, the text slows down to introduce him: a long line of fathers, name after name, back to Aaron the chief priest. Then a job title.
In the King James words: "he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given."
He comes up from Babylon with the king's permission and a company of returning exiles, and the good hand of his God, the text says, was upon him. Then one sentence about what he set his heart on.

teach.h: SEEK IT, DO IT, TEACH IT.
teach.b: Here it is: "For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments." Three verbs, in an order. Seek.

The Hebrew verb is lidrosh, to search, to ask. Some readers hear in it the word midrash, the old Jewish way of searching a text for more than its surface. Ezra doesn't just read the law; he goes looking in it.

teach.h: DO IT BEFORE YOU TEACH IT.
teach.b: Before he teaches anyone, he does it himself; the verse puts the doing before a single word of teaching reaches anyone else. Teach. Only then does it go outward, to the people.
And notice where it starts: he prepared his heart. Not his pen, not his scroll. Study begins as a direction you set inside.
Today's word is what he was: a sofer, a scribe. The word is still in use.

teach.h: A SOFER STILL WRITES BY HAND.
teach.b: A sofer writes a Torah scroll by hand, letter by letter, with a quill on parchment, and tradition asks that a scroll for public reading be written that way, by someone who sits down and sets their heart to it.

how: A sofer is a trained Jewish scribe who writes Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot by hand with a quill and ink on parchment, following detailed laws for every letter, and Ezra is remembered in Jewish tradition as Ezra the Scribe.

o: a teacher who explains the law to children
a priest who serves at the Temple's altar
a scribe, who writes a Torah scroll by hand

games.q: seek, do, teach — tap the pairs.
p: search the law of the LORD
live it before you teach it
a scribe, still writing by hand

s: Ezra is called a ready scribe in the law of Moses
"he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses."
in Ezra 7:10, teaching comes before doing
the order is seek, do, teach. he does it before he teaches it.
scribes who write Torah scrolls by hand are only a thing of the past
a sofer today still writes Torah scrolls, tefillin and mezuzot by hand.

games.q: Ezra 7:10 says Ezra prepared his heart for three things. in what order does the verse give them?
games.why: seek the law, do it, and teach it. doing comes before teaching.

practice: Take one line you trust, today's verse from Ezra or one from a book you keep near, and seek: turn it over and ask it one question.
Then do: find one small, specific way to live it; then teach: think how you'd pass it on in a sentence. If you pray, ask in words from your tradition for a prepared heart.

wordCard.voice: Sofer. A scribe. Ezra was called a ready scribe in the law of Moses, and a sofer today still writes the Torah by hand. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a scribe. Ezra is called a sofer in Ezra 7:6, and the word is still used for Jewish scribes today.
